newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-INJURED BOLDON PULLS OUT OF GOLDEN GALA.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-INJURED BOLDON PULLS OUT OF GOLDEN GALA.

text.p: Trinidad's Ato Boldon, the fastest man over 100 metres this year, withdrew injured from the Golden Gala international athletics meeting on Wednesday and said he would not race again until the end of June.
"Three steps out of the blocks in Saint-Denis I knew something was wrong," he told a news conference.
"Luckily I finished without something more serious happening. But the best thing for the world championships is for me to go home and return at the end of June.
"I do have to go home and take care of my leg."
Boldon came fourth in the 100 metres race in France on Monday, behind Namibia's Frankie Fredericks. The world championships are in Athens in August.
The two rivals had been due to race each other in the 200 metres at Rome's Olympic Stadium on Thursday.
Boldon said he had felt a twinge in his left leg before leaving home in Los Angeles last Thursday.

"If as a sprinter you decide not to compete because of every little twinge, you would have a very short season," said the 23-year-old, who clocked the sixth fastest time ever of 9.89 seconds last month in Modesto, California, explaining why he came.
Boldon said he would stay to watch the meeting and intended to return to competition at the end of the month.

Organisers of the Golden Gala have billed the meeting as a return to basics after two unsatisfactory million-dollar extravaganzas at the weekend but Boldon's withdrawal robbed the gathering of one of its big draws.

"Toronto was fairground athletics. We on the other hand are offering real athletics, full of interesting duels in a programme that I believe to be extremely valid," said Italian athletic federation president Gianni Gola this week.
Donovan Bailey won his head-to-head clash against Michael Johnson in Toronto on Sunday after the American pulled up 30 metres from the line in their 150 metres showdown.
Boldon did not share Gola's view.
"I enjoyed it," he said. "I can't remember when was the last time that I enjoyed a track and field match that much."
But Fredericks put a different perspective on it.
"I'm not doing this to be liked, to be famous or to be a star," he said, when asked if he felt left out.

"I'm fortunate to be here. A lot of my countrymen did not have the chance to compete because of apartheid and all that we went through. I think I am blessed to be here. I'm taking care of my family, the things that are important to me."
There is $50,000 on offer for a world record but organisers prefer to highlight the attractions of Rome in the summer and the crowd will still have many stars to watch.
World indoor champion Hicham El Guerrouj of Morocco, who failed in an attempt to break Morceli's 1,500 metres world record at Saint-Denis on Monday, will run again.
World steeplechase champion Moses Kiptanui of Kenya is racing the 3,000 metres in the closing event of the evening and promised a race to remember.
"I'm trying tomorrow to race a sub eight minutes again," he said. "I want to do it before the world championships."
Cuban high jump world record holder Javier Sotomayor will be present for only his second event since a disappointing 1996 Olympics and subsequent injury problems.
Russia's double Olympic champion Svetlana Masterkova has her first real challenge of the season in the women's 800 metres against Cuba's world champion Ana Quirot.
She also has other matters on her mind. "Shoes. In Rome I'd like to buy a nice pair of shoes," the Russian said.
